content: CHD3, or Chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding protein 3, is an enzyme encoded by the CHD3 gene in humans. This gene produces a protein that belongs to the CHD family, which is defined by the presence of chromo domains (chromatin organization modifier domains) and SNF2-related helicase/ATPase domains. The CHD3 protein is a critical component of the Mi-2/NuRD complex, a histone deacetylase complex that plays a key role in chromatin remodeling by deacetylating histones. Chromatin remodeling is a fundamental process required for various cellular functions, including transcription regulation. Autoantibodies targeting CHD3 have been identified in a subset of patients with dermatomyositis, an inflammatory muscle disease. Additionally, three alternatively spliced transcripts of the CHD3 gene have been described, each encoding distinct isoforms of the protein. Mutations in the CHD3 gene are associated with a neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by macrocephaly (an abnormally large head) and deficits in speech and language development. CHD3 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1), histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2), and SERBP1 (SERPINE1 mRNA binding protein 1).
